Subject: Procurement readiness check-in: PR intake, marketplace vs PO/card, Coupa/Ariba mapping

Hi Sarah — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and recommended next steps focused on procurement readiness so your ops team can ingest Redwood quickly.

Key ask from the call: confirm whether FalconPay will: 1) route Redwood through a marketplace listing (Coupa/Ariba marketplace) 2) raise POs through your Coupa/Ariba instance to Redwood as a vendor, or 3) use corporate card for initial small-value purchases.

Attached are two quick artifacts to speed intake: PR_Template_Coupa.csv (sample line items + cost codes) and Vendor_Setup_Guide_Ariba_v1.pdf (vendor ID mapping fields we need). If you prefer, we can share a minimal billing-only vendor packet instead.

Suggested next steps (1–2 business-day cadence):
- You: confirm procurement path (marketplace | PO | card) and preferred contact for vendor setup (name/email).
- If PO path: share Vendor Legal Name, Remit Address, Tax ID and preferred payment terms (Net 30/Net 45).
- If marketplace: confirm vendor listing search name and any marketplace SKU we should map to.
- Redwood: we will open a vendor intake ticket with our finance/ops team and share the Coupa/Ariba mapping; we can also provide a short sample invoice if useful.

Please reply with which path you’d like to pursue and I’ll start the intake.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Hi Sarah — answering inline: 

- Marketplace listing: Redwood is listed on a subset of marketplaces but not every buyer marketplace. We may or may not have a FalconPay-specific vendor ID yet. If you want to try marketplace first, please search "Redwood Inference" in Coupa; if you can’t find us I’ll start a vendor request.

- Vendor setup lead time: typically 3–10 business days from intake on your side (depending on finance checks and tax paperwork). We try to expedite pilot vendors under $10k in value.

- Card vs PO: we accept corporate card for initial pilot invoices; however your AP policy may still require a PR/PO for internal approvals. For recurring production usage we recommend PO path for easier reconciliation and SSO-based integration.

Actions I will take now:
1) Open an internal vendor intake ticket with our finance/operations team and assign it to procurement ops — ticket ITSM-2247 (I will forward updates).
2) Loop in Markus on commercial/payment terms if FalconPay requests a non-standard SLA/term set.
3) Share sample invoice template if your team wants to see how line items map to cost centers.

If you prefer we can do a short follow-up call with your procurement ops to walk through the vendor-setup flow.

Thanks — Vanessa
